title.value: Signal diffusion along connectome gradients and inter-hub routing differentially contribute to dynamic human brain function
title.justification: The title captures the central theme of the paper which is about exploring how signal diffusion along connectome gradients and inter-hub routing contributes to human brain function.
title.quote:
Signal diffusion along connectome gradients and inter-hub routing
differentially contribute to dynamic human brain function

analysis.description: The paper investigates the mechanisms behind the dynamic transitions of human brain functional states within the framework of structural connectome organization, utilizing manifold learning and Hidden Markov Models (HMMs) to understand these transitions anchored in sensorimotor and transmodal cortical systems.

type.justification: The paper describes experimental investigations conducted using advanced imaging techniques (dMRI, fMRI) across a large cohort, with findings based on data analysis, particularly focusing on transient functional brain states and structural network organization.
type.quote:
Studying a large cohort of healthy adults (n = 326), we
capitalized on manifold learning techniques that identify low dimensional representations of structural connec-
tome organization and we decomposed neurophysiological activity into distinct functional states and their tran-
sition patterns using Hidden Markov Models.

name.justification: The paper predominantly focuses on the analysis of brain structure and function relationships using neuroimaging techniques, which are central to the field of Neuroscience.
name.quote: Understanding how the structure of the cortex gives rise to ongoing cognitive function is a key aim for systems neuroscience

name.justification: The paper extensively deals with the structural connectome of the brain and its role in cognitive functions and transitions between neural states.
name.quote:

name.justification: Hidden Markov Models were used to model distinct brain states and transition patterns, showing its significant role in the analysis performed in the paper.

is_contributed.justification: Hidden Markov Models are established models and were not specifically introduced by this paper.
is_contributed.quote:
One method that can resolve functional dynamics is the Hidden Markov Model (HMM), a gen-
erative probabilistic framework that identifies time-varying brain states and associated connectivity profiles

is_executed.justification: Hidden Markov Models were actively applied to estimate dynamic states and corresponding connectivity.
is_executed.quote:
we decomposed neurophysiological activity into distinct functional states and their tran-

is_compared.justification: The paper does not focus on comparing HMM to other models numerically.
is_compared.quote:
We did not make a-priori predictions how structurally-defined low di-
mensional manifolds may relate to measures of functional dynamics, as
whole-brain gradients derived from dMRI tractography data have not
been systematically studied in humans nor integrated with HMM data.
